A table of geometries as vector tiles

Source: R/tiles.R
rr_tiles_table.Rd

Makes a tile function for a "vector" rr_layer() from a table of points, lines or areas: the table is copied once into a temporary DuckDB table in web mercator, with each feature's bounds, and each tile is cut from it by DuckDB (ST_AsMVT()). Every feature carries kind ("point", "line" or "area") and the properties.

Usage

rr_tiles_table(
  x,
  geometry = "geometry",
  lon = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  properties = NULL,
  layer = "features",
  points = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A lazy DuckDB table or a data frame: a geometry column (DuckDB's GEOMETRY, or WKB), or lon and lat.

geometry

The geometry column; or lon, lat for points from two columns.

lon, lat

The position columns, for points.

properties

The columns each feature carries. A vector tile holds text, numbers and logicals only, so a factor, date or time is carried as text, a small integer as an integer and a decimal as a double.

layer

The tile layer of the features.

points

The tile layer of a point on every feature (ST_PointOnSurface()), for the zooms where an area is too small to see; NULL for none.

Value

A function of z, x, y returning a tile (raw bytes), with the number of features as its count attribute, the temporary table's name as its table attribute, and as tiles_at a function of a zoom giving the tiles that hold a feature (x, y), by which rr_bundle() writes only those.

Examples

# \donttest{
tiles <- rr_tiles_table(rr_example("dansk_harbours"),
  properties = "SI_HARB", points = "harbour_points")
attr(tiles, "count")
#> [1] 942
length(tiles(7, 68, 39))
#> [1] 1522
# }
